subject: Latency spike after model v9c rollout — mitigation & authorization
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightpath.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@brightpath.com
Date: 2028-01-18T14:06:00Z
Subject: Sudden p95 latency spike after v9c deployment

Hi Ben / Redwood support,

We started seeing a major p95 latency regression right after your announced v9c rollout at ~13:45 UTC. Our customer-facing API (BrightPath Clinical Search) is hitting ~1.9s p95 compared to typical ~420ms. This is causing slow page loads and several error-rate complaints from users.

Quick details:
- Region: us-east-1
- Model variant: redwood-model-v9c (pinned in our prod route)
- First observed: 2028-01-18T13:48:22Z
- Impact: 18% increase in 95th percentile response time, some timeouts in our downstream worker pool

Can you confirm if the v9c rollout is related and whether you can immediately revert or fallback to the previous stable variant (v9b)? We need an ETA and an indication of whether this will require downtime or schema changes on our side.

I've attached a Grafana screenshot and our initial traces. Please escalate—this is high priority for BrightPath.

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Sr. Product Manager, BrightPath Health
Attachments: grafana_p95_screenshot.png (image), bp_initial_traces.json (trace bundle)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightpath.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T14:21:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p95 latency spike after v9c deployment

Forwarding BrightPath's alert — they saw an immediate p95 spike after our v9c rollout. Customer requests a rollback/fallback to v9b ASAP.

Context: BrightPath is a high-volume production account (BP-4209) on dedicated capacity. Rolling back a model variant on dedicated pools is possible but we need SRE + infra sign-off because some caches (KV prefix caches) and batch sizing may change the expected latency profile.

Can you two triage and propose the fastest safe mitigation (variant fallback, routing override, or temporary scaling)? Also copy me on the mitigation timeline and whether we need leadership approval for a temporary SLA carveout/credit.

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightpath.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95 latency spike after v9c deployment

Ben / team,

I've pulled the traces and kernel metrics — the regression line up with an attention-kernel scheduling change in v9c that increases tail latency under BrightPath's sequence-length distribution and batch-size pattern. Key findings:
- Elevated token-level compute on long-form prefixes (two hotspots around 0.9s and 1.4s).
- KV cache hit-rate unchanged; not a cache eviction problem.
- Canary traffic to v9b shows expected ~430ms p95.

Mitigation options (fastest to slowest):
1) Variant fallback: route BrightPath's production route to v9b (compatible weights). This is the least risky for correctness; estimated change window 30–45 minutes to update routing + warm caches. No model data migration required.
2) Routing override to a lower-capacity tier temporarily: reduces throughput, may increase cost and throttle some requests — not ideal.
3) Roll-forward with a targeted patch to attention kernel (longer path, requires QA and new build).

I'm attaching aggregate traces and a short runbook for the rollback path. If we choose (1) we should notify BrightPath and request a temporary SLA credit notification while we stabilize. I can execute the variant fallback once SRE authorizes and we have leadership sign-off on the SLA communication.

Attachments: bp_v9c_p95_traces.zip, runbook_sla_rollback_v2.pdf

—Michael
Michael Grant
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightpath.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95 latency spike after v9c deployment

Michael / Ben,

I agree with Michael's assessment. From an SRE perspective, variant fallback to v9b is the quickest safe mitigation. Operational notes:
- Because BrightPath is on Dedicated, we need to schedule routing update on their dedicated pool's control plane; it's a low-risk config change but requires a maintenance window flag.
- I'll open an internal change with the ops gating checklist:
  - Pre-change health snapshot (already captured)
  - Routing override to v9b
  - Monitor p95 for 30 minutes post-change
  - Roll forward configuration if mismatch detected

Estimated timeline: 45 minutes from authorization to completion (includes cache warm). If the upgrade takes longer than 90 minutes, we'll trigger incident escalation per RW-OPS runbook.

I've created Jira RW-8421 and linked the support ticket (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-8421). We need a leadership approval for:
- Executing the variant fallback on dedicated capacity now.
- Notifying BrightPath with a temporary SLA credit offer (per our enterprise escalation policy) — approval needed because this is a deviation from standard auto-fallback.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightpath.com>
Date: 2028-01-19T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95 latency spike after v9c deployment

All — thanks for the quick analysis. Authorize the variant fallback to v9b on BrightPath's dedicated pool immediately.

Conditions:
- Proceed with Rishi's change checklist and monitor p95 for at least 30 minutes after completion.
- Offer BrightPath a 10% temporary SLA credit for the affected window and send a short incident summary once we stabilize. Ben, please coordinate the customer comms; include the Grafana snapshot and the expected completion time.
- Log all change steps and time in RW-8421. If the rollback takes >60 minutes, escalate to me and the on-call for further coordination.

Ben — you have authorization to communicate the mitigation plan and the offer. Keep me posted with a quick status update once p95 is back within baseline.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
